references.text: In [ref:Esek 36:25-27|Ezekiel 36:25-27], God promises to sprinkle clean water over His people and give them a new spirit. This is a central Old Testament background for Jesus' words about being born of water and the Spirit, linking cleansing (water) with the renewing power of the Spirit.

In [ref:Esek 37:1-14|Ezekiel 37:1-14], God's Spirit (ruach) breathes life into dry bones. This vision illustrates the life-giving power of the Spirit, which Jesus refers to when He speaks about being born of the Spirit.

In [ref:Jes 44:3-5|Isaiah 44:3-5], God promises to pour water on the thirsty land and His Spirit over Israel's offspring, leading to new spiritual life. This aligns with Jesus' connection between water and the Spirit as a condition for entering God's kingdom.
In [ref:Joh 3:3|John 3:3], Jesus says that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again. Verse 5 expands on this by specifying that the new birth occurs of water and the Spirit.

[ref:Joh 1:12-13|John 1:12-13] speaks of being born of God—not of blood, the will of the flesh, or the will of man. This anticipates the theme of divine, spiritual birth that Jesus explains in His conversation with Nicodemus.
[ref:Tit 3:5-7|Titus 3:5-7] refers to salvation through "the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit", a direct parallel to Jesus' words about being born of water and the Spirit.

In [ref:Ef 5:25-27|Ephesians 5:25-27], Christ cleanses the church "by the washing of water with the word". This connection between water and spiritual cleansing illuminates Jesus' teaching on the role of water and the Spirit in regeneration.

In [ref:1 Pet 1:3|1 Peter 1:3], God is praised for having regenerated us to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. The theme of regeneration is central here as well, expanding on what it means to be born again by the Spirit.

[ref:1 Pet 1:23|1 Peter 1:23] states that believers are reborn, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God. This underscores the spiritual nature of regeneration, in line with John 3:5.

In [ref:1 Joh 5:6-8|1 John 5:6-8], the Spirit, the water, and the blood bear witness together. The connection between water and the Spirit as testimony in John expands on the close relationship between these two elements in Jesus' teaching about regeneration.

In [ref:Apg 2:38|Acts 2:38], Peter calls for repentance and baptism for the forgiveness of sins, with the promise of the gift of the Holy Spirit. Baptism (water) and the Spirit are directly linked here, just as Jesus does in His talk with Nicodemus.

In [ref:Rom 6:3-4|Romans 6:3-4], Paul explains that baptism unites the believer with Christ's death and resurrection, so that one walks in new life. This expands on how water baptism is connected to the new life Jesus mentions in John 3:5.
